section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the three interpretations of "teva" (nature) correspond to three distinct concepts: nature as continuous miracles, as the divine life-force animating the world, and as the power that creates ex nihilo beyond intellect.
section.t: And it is explained in the discourses,
that the three aforementioned interpretations are three distinct matters.
For according to the interpretation of the Chacham Tzvi that nature is continuous miracles,
there the term "nature" refers to the conduct of the world.
And according to the interpretation that "teva" is from the term "matbea" (coin), that the Holy One, blessed be He, imprinted every person with the seal of Adam HaRishon,
and the Rambam explained
that the seal of Adam HaRishon is the form of the human species by which a human is human,
that the intention of "form of the human species" is
(primarily)
the spiritual form within him—
there the term "nature" refers to the divine life-force within the world,
which is the soul of the world.
And the connection of this matter to nature in its simple sense is,
that the form and nature of every created being is according to the manner of the divine life-force within it.

And according to the interpretation that "teva" is a borrowed term for anything not based on reason and intellect—there the term "nature" refers to the divine power that brings every created being into existence from nothing to something,
for bringing into existence from nothing to something is beyond intellect.
For this, that the divine life-force animates the created beings,
has a place in intellect,
and the matter of nature
(according to the interpretation that nature is that which is not based on reason and intellect)
is in the bringing into existence of created beings,
for creation of something from nothing is beyond intellect.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two interpretations of nature—as the divine life-force and as the creative power—both relate to the meaning of "teva" as immersion, since the divine power is concealed within creation.
section.t: And it is explained in the discourses,
that the two interpretations
(the matters)
of nature,
that it is the divine life-force that animates the created beings and that it is the divine power that brings the created beings into existence from nothing to something,
are related to the interpretation that "teva" is from the term "teviah" (immersion),
"they sank"
in the Sea of Reeds.
For just as in simple immersion,
when something is immersed in water,
the water covers the thing immersed in them,
so too is it with the divine life-force that is clothed in the created beings to animate them,
that the created beings cover the divine life-force that is clothed within them.
And likewise with the divine power that brings the created beings into existence from nothing to something,
for the matter of nature within it is also from the term "immersion,"
since the bringing into existence is in a manner of concealment and hiding,
that the creative power is concealed and hidden within the created beings,
therefore the matter of "teva" from the term "immersion" and concealment applies to it.
